q: Sullivan's no-wandering-domains theorem (1985) states that for a rational map f: ℂ̂ → ℂ̂:
opts: All Fatou components are eventually periodic
Every wandering domain maps to a periodic cycle of Fatou components (no proper wandering domains exist)
The Fatou set is always connected
Every Fatou component is simply connected
exp: Sullivan's theorem (using quasiconformal surgery): rational maps have no wandering Fatou components—every Fatou component eventually maps into a periodic cycle. Before Sullivan, wandering domains were only ruled out for specific classes. This was a landmark application of quasiconformal deformations.
